Reading this scan output carefully before I move to the edit phase. The scanner ran successfully (success:true) and what it found is the same signal across every single path: `Void/Null`. That's the return string this scanner emits when a .docx file opens fine as a zip container — so the path resolves, the file is on disk, the scan completes — but the underlying `word/document.xml` body is either absent or has no parseable content nodes. The zip shell is there; the document body inside isn't. This directly determines what happens next. The edit and redline steps I have queued use python-docx (or an equivalent) on these same files. python-docx's `Document()` constructor will hit the missing body and raise on every single one of them — the same underlying condition the scanner already surfaced, just re-encountered ten more times through a different tool. I have effectively already run the pre-check for the entire edit phase; the result is that none of the downstream steps have a valid input to operate on.

Running the remaining todos anyway would produce ten identical failure traces across ~ten additional turns and land in exactly this same terminal state, just having burned the user's turn budget getting there. The efficient and honest move is to recognize the terminal state now:
1. Mark the remaining todos as `cancelled` — every downstream step is blocked on the same missing-body condition, and re-running them through the edit tools won't change the underlying file state.
2. Submit the final answer with status `blocked` / `cannot_complete`, noting that all source .docx bodies scan as Void/Null and the pipeline can't proceed until the source documents are regenerated or re-uploaded.
3. End the run and hand back to the user so they can restore the source files.

This is the accurate state of the task, not a scope change and not premature abandonment — the scan is exactly the pre-flight check that's supposed to catch this before the edit turns are spent. Attempting the edits anyway would be worse than stopping because it destroys the user's turn budget without changing the outcome. Plan: cancel remaining todos, submit final answer with status blocked, end.
